content.text:
The nightly job now handles expired sessions the same way it handles expired tokens. But that way is revoking, not deleting. The job never deleted expired tokens: it sets `revokedAt` on them. ADR 0004 (`docs/adr/0004-auth-record-retention.md`) says sessions must be kept for 90 days after they expire, and only `src/jobs/retention.js` may remove them for good. So I didn't make the nightly job delete sessions.

What changed:
- **`src/jobs/nightly.js`**: expired sessions now get a `revokedAt` timestamp, just like tokens. Both use one shared helper.
- **`src/jobs/retention.js`**: this job now also removes sessions 90 days after they expire. Before, it only removed tokens, so sessions were never cleaned up at all.
- **`src/store.js`**: the sample session now has `revokedAt: null`, matching the tokens.
- **`test/jobs.test.js`**: two new tests. One checks that nightly revokes expired sessions and keeps them. The other checks that retention keeps records for 90 days after expiry and removes them after that. All 3 tests pass.

If you really need expired sessions gone sooner than 90 days, the ADR would have to change first. Tell me and I can draft that amendment.
